# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have read the defusal manual. The bomb requires pressing the key marked with the symbol ⵘ first; pressing any other key or touching the bomb out of turn detonates the fuse. After that key is pressed, the defusal depends on the color of the light below, which determines which colored wire must be cut (blue light -> cut yellow wire; red light -> cut red wire; yellow light -> cut green wire).

However, I cannot speak, nor can I touch the bomb. I can only send gestures to Deaf, who can see markings on the bomb and can speak to Blind, who can physically feel and manipulate the bomb. 

At this opening turn, neither Blind nor Deaf has reported what they feel or see. Because a sign has no meaning until a protocol has been established, any gestures I make now would be ungrounded and easily misinterpreted. I will wait for Blind to describe the physical layout and Deaf to describe the visual markings and propose or enable an agreed signaling protocol.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. Bomb components: DISPLAY, LIGHT, KEYPAD (slots 1 to 4, 1 digit needed), WIRES (positions 1, 2, 3). My actions: act(op='press', slot=N) for N=1..4, and act(op='cut', position=N) for N=1..3. I cannot see gestures, only hear speech. Have Deaf speak the exact actions for me to execute.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is yellow. There are 3 wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. Keypad has 4 buttons and needs 1 digit: button 1 is five dots in an X pattern like the 5 on a die, button 2 is a mirrored backwards capital D, button 3 is a spiral swirl, button 4 is a mirrored backwards capital B. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do, and I will speak the instructions to Blind.

I have reviewed the manual and the bomb details provided by Deaf. 

The manual specifies:
- Press the key that wears ⵘ first. Button 1 is described by Deaf as "five dots in an X pattern like the 5 on a die", which matches the character ⵘ.
- Any other touch while it waits is the fuse, so no wire should be cut or other button pressed before button 1 is pressed.
- Blind explicitly needs Deaf to speak the exact action `act(op='press', slot=1)`.

To instruct Deaf clearly and unambiguously without risk of confusion:
- Gesturing `👇` indicates "press".
- Gesturing `☝` indicates "slot 1" (button 1).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝"])
```

TURN 3

Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: do NOT touch anything yet, please wait. Mute: I received your gestures [👇 ☝]. Because a single wrong action detonates the bomb, please clarify: if you mean CUT WIRE 1, gesture 👍. If you mean PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON 1, gesture 👎. If you mean something else, gesture 👌.

Deaf has asked for clarification on the gestures received:
- If I mean CUT WIRE 1, gesture 👍.
- If I mean PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON 1, gesture 👎.
- If I mean something else, gesture 👌.

The defusal manual explicitly mandates pressing the key bearing ⵘ (button 1) first before any wire cutting or other actions. Therefore, the required action is PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON 1.

I will gesture 👎 to confirm PRESS KEYPAD BUTTON 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I told Blind to press Keypad Button 1. Gesture 👍 when it's done or if that's everything.

I have reviewed the manual and the current sequence of turns:

1. Deaf has instructed Blind to press Keypad Button 1.
2. In the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), Blind acts next in Round 4 and will execute the press on button 1.
3. Defusal is not finished after pressing Keypad Button 1: the manual specifies that following the key press, the light indicates which wire must be cut.
4. Since the defusal is not complete, I should not gesture 👍 ("done / that's everything"). Deaf will observe the bomb's state after Blind presses the button and report back at the end of this round.

Therefore, I will wait.

```
wait()
```

Deaf says: The keypad opened! Current bomb status: Keypad shows entered 1 and is open. Display shows 0. Indicator light is yellow. Wires: 1 is red, 2 is yellow, 3 is green. Mute, what should Blind do next? If cut wire 1, gesture ☝. If cut wire 2, gesture ✌. If cut wire 3, gesture 🤟. If bomb is defused / do nothing, gesture 👍. If something else, gesture 👌. Blind: please hold and do not touch anything yet.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute: I told Blind to cut wire 3.

I have communicated the instruction to cut wire 3 (the green wire, corresponding to the yellow light), and Deaf has passed this instruction on to Blind. Blind will execute the cut on wire 3 this round. I will wait for the outcome.

```
wait()
```
